name: Wright Flyer (1903)
headline: wingspan
subtitle: The original airplane at the National Air and Space Museum
description: The 1903 Wright Flyer, built by Wilbur and Orville Wright, made its first flights on December 17, 1903, at Kitty Hawk, North Carolina. It is a canard biplane of wood and muslin with a 12-horsepower engine driving two pusher propellers through chains. The Smithsonian gives its wingspan as 12.3 m (40 ft 4 in) and its empty weight as 274 kg.

facts.text: Orville Wright made the first flight on December 17, 1903: 12 seconds covering 36 m (120 ft).
The fourth and last flight that day, flown by Wilbur, covered 255.6 m (852 ft) in 59 seconds.
A single 12-horsepower, four-cylinder Wright engine drove two pusher propellers through a sprocket-and-chain transmission.

sources.publisher: Smithsonian National Air and Space Museum
